messages.text: How do changes in AI data centers technology affect the measurement capability required from Signaling / Non-signaling Tester?

AI data center technology changes mainly shift measurement needs toward high-voltage power, high-speed interconnect, PCB signal integrity, cooling/leak reliability, and only secondarily toward wireless signaling/non-signaling test when AI-enabled 5G/6G/WLAN devices are involved.[5][6][15][19][21][25]
| AI data center technology change | Measurement capability implication for Signaling / Non-signaling Tester |
|---|---|
| AI racks are moving from `48 V` toward `800 V` or `±400Vdc` as rack power rises toward `200 kW`–`250 kW` and eventually MW-class levels.[15] | This is not a core signaling/non-signaling wireless test problem; it points to power, safety, precharge, discharge, and eFuse validation needs outside the cited CMX500 wireless feature set.[15][21] |
| High-voltage server boards require precharge before connection to the HVDC bus, timely discharge when removed, and eFuse fault cut-off.[15] | Signaling/non-signaling testers would need integration with external power/event instrumentation if used in a broader rack validation flow, because the cited CMX500 capabilities are wireless signaling, TX, throughput, BLER, PER, fading, AWGN, and IP/application tests.[15][21] |
| AI server PCB trends move toward high layer count, large area, high-speed transmission, M8 CCL, HVLP copper, low-Dk, low-loss, high-thermal designs, 30–40 layers, and 12–14 aspect ratio processes.[5][12] | The primary measurement need becomes high-speed electrical/PCB SI such as IL, TDR, high-speed trace, and PDN Target Z, not traditional wireless signaling/non-signaling testing.[10][12] |
| Data center connectivity covers high-speed electrical interconnect, optical interconnect, fiber deployment, rack power distribution, busbar, liquid cooling, and leak detection.[6] | Signaling/non-signaling testers are only relevant to the wireless/protocol-facing parts of this ecosystem, while many AI data center changes require interconnect, power, thermal, and leak-detection measurement capabilities.[6][19][21] |
| The R&S CMX500 is a one-box network emulation and measurement test solution for device testing across LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD, and TDD.[21] | For AI-related wireless devices or modules, the required signaling capability should include NR FR1/FR2 signaling, LTE signaling, WLAN signaling, TX measurements, fading, AWGN, BLER, CSI report, throughput, PER, application test, IP traffic analysis, IMS/audio/POLQA, and remote automation by GUI, scripting, Python XLAPI, or SCPI.[21] |
| A 6G AI proof-of-concept used the CMX500 one-box tester to show significant downlink throughput gain in AI-based wireless transmission versus conventional non-AI technology.[25] | For AI-native wireless evolution, signaling/non-signaling testers need to measure AI-related throughput gains and user-experience effects such as video streaming performance, where supported by the test scenario.[25] |
【推論】For AI data center power and rack evolution, signaling/non-signaling testers should not be positioned as the main measurement tool unless the device under test includes wireless connectivity, because the cited AI data center changes are HVDC, PCB, interconnect, power, and cooling focused, while the cited CMX500 scope is wireless network emulation and device measurement.[6][15][19][21]
【推論】For AI-enabled 5G/6G/WLAN modules used around data center infrastructure, the tester capability should emphasize signaling plus throughput, BLER/PER, fading/AWGN, TX, IP/application, and automation coverage, because these are the supported CMX500 functions and the RAW 6G AI demo highlights AI-based downlink throughput gain.[21][25]
【推論】For non-signaling production or regression use, the passages support focusing only on the cited TX and WLAN TX measurement aspects, but they do not provide a separate non-signaling tester model, option code, or AI data center-specific non-signaling requirement.[21]
